terra.problem: The shower comparison fails the joke logic test: a lukewarm shower can still get someone clean and be comfortable.
“Jesus means it to land” assigns Him an intention the text does not state.
The passage says Jesus stands at the door; it does not identify it as their door.
Matthew 13:46 speaks of one pearl of great value, not pearls of great value.
“Good memory on the pearls” assumes the baker remembered that parable, which Papa Dorin has not been told.
The passage does not say the church thinks it can see just fine.
Jesus says He rebukes and disciplines those He loves; the verse does not explicitly name love as the reason He does so.
The final sentence leaves out the condition that the person also opens the door.
The passage says Jesus will come in and dine, but does not say He will sit down.
Revelation 3:12 mentions the name of the new Jerusalem, but does not promise a home inside it. The selected answer cannot be attributed to that letter.
